title: B14-MT-150-Restore-The-Deleted-Test-Coverage-The-SurrealDB-Port-Did-Not-Carry-Over

lifecycle.creation_reason: Commit 4f92cc25 (the src-side PostgreSQL removal, MT-136/137/138 territory) deleted 26 test files. MT-141 inherited a tree with those tests already gone. A coverage sweep across BOTH src/ and tests/ found that of 57 deleted tests, 3 covered removed behaviour and 4 are covered elsewhere, but 47 cover production behaviour that is still live and either has no proof anywhere (33) or only partial proof (14). Deleting a test to reach a green compile is the exact failure MT-141 exists to prevent, so this coverage cannot be silently dropped. Under Operator decision 2026-09-10 (fast close), MT-141 closes on a complete disposition and this microtask carries the restoration as tracked, non-silent debt.
lifecycle.why_a_separate_microtask: Three reasons. (1) A predecessor microtask deleted them, not MT-141. (2) Seventeen items need an axum+reqwest HTTP harness and the whole set is 47 tests; folding that into MT-141 would hold MT-148 and the WP hostage. (3) Three items are blocked on a PRODUCT defect (no production store implements MemoryCapsuleIpcStore) and cannot be ported by any tests/-only microtask. Operator chose the fast path explicitly.

operator_decision_2026_09_10.authority: Operator reply: 'fast, close 141 with your exceptions implemented.'
operator_decision_2026_09_10.why_those_three: They guard a live privilege-escalation check at src/api/knowledge_documents.rs:467 that had zero coverage at any layer. Restored into tests/knowledge_documents_api_tests.rs reusing its existing doc_server harness.

lifecycle.urgency: HIGH for the three security-relevant items and the Loom rollback variants; MEDIUM otherwise.

operator_direction_2026_09_10.note: Operator states repo governance will be abandoned soon and that only state recovery and status matter. Consequence for follow-ups: do not build the missing receipt emitter as governance work; MT-150 and the two routed product defects are state-recovery debt to carry into whatever replaces repo governance, not rituals to complete here.

scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. No SQLite or PostgreSQL may be added, restored, imported or referenced as a live backend. Original test names containing 'postgres' or '_pg_' MUST be renamed on port; the name is not the proof intent.
harness_reuse_required: HTTP route tests: reuse route_server / doc_server / identity_headers in tests/knowledge_documents_api_tests.rs, or the serve() idiom in tests/atelier_loom_projection_api_tests.rs. Do NOT author a new HTTP harness.
Embedded store tests: reuse tests/surreal_test_store_support/ and tests/atelier_surreal_support/ (note: atelier_surreal_support requires HANDSHAKE_WORKSPACE_ROOT to be set, hard assert at mod.rs:42).

Loom rollback variants (rollback_variant=true): the PostgreSQL originals injected a trigger to force ledger-append failure. SurrealDB has no equivalent; solve the injection ONCE centrally (a test-support fault-injection seam) and reuse it for all six, rather than six ad-hoc mechanisms.
acceptance_criteria: AC-150-1: every item in restoration_set is either ported with all original assertions preserved, or carries a typed disposition of BLOCKED_ON_PRODUCT_DEFECT naming the defect id. No item may be silently dropped or weakened.
AC-150-2: no ported test depends on sqlx, PostgreSQL, psql, PG DSN env vars, SQLite or PL/pgSQL (same anti-laundering test as AC-141-1).
AC-150-3: ported durability tests (survives_restart, rolls_back) prove behaviour across a real store close-and-reopen, not against mocks.
AC-150-4: every ported test runs green on the pinned toolchain with per-run isolation, with HANDSHAKE_WORKSPACE_ROOT set to an isolated per-run directory.

AC-150-5: the six manual_rows-family PARTIAL items restore the distinguishing assert_schema_fields_are_real cross-check (model_manual() CommandReference schema_fields vs real runtime struct fields), which is the one guarantee the existing partial coverage does not make.
AC-150-6: the two reduced_confidence items (mt123, mt125) receive a full assertion-by-assertion diff against the recovered deleted body before their port is designed.
proof_targets: PT-150-1: per-test disposition table (PORTED | BLOCKED_ON_PRODUCT_DEFECT) with the new test path for each PORTED item.
PT-150-2: cargo test output for every new/changed target with zero failures and nonzero executed count, run with HANDSHAKE_WORKSPACE_ROOT set and no concurrent cargo lane.
PT-150-3: the repo-wide forbidden-database scan (AC-141-1 method) over the changed files.
execution_constraints: One cargo process per lane. Do not run a second cargo lane concurrently on this host; suite-run-1 under MT-141 recorded three timeout-shaped false failures from exactly that.
Use --features surreal-test-support,test-utils; the tests tree does not compile without them.
Owner-scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/<WP>/MT-150/<owner>/ reached through a short junction; this WP id exceeds Windows MAX_PATH otherwise (link.exe LNK1104).
scope.risk_if_missed: Live production routes and a scheduling state machine stay untested; the Loom atomic-receipt contract has no rollback proof; security-relevant stage/activity-span boundaries stay uncovered.

blocked_by_product_defects.summary: MemoryCapsuleIpcStore (src/memory/ipc.rs:37) has zero production implementors; only InMemoryCapsuleStore test doubles exist. Three restoration items cannot be ported until a real store implements the trait. Needs its own src/-owning microtask.
blocked_by_product_defects.provenance: A PostgresMemoryCapsuleStore implementor existed at src/memory/persistence_postgres.rs:673 before 4f92cc25 and was deleted with it; no Surreal-backed replacement was written. LANE-M documents what a SurrealMemoryCapsuleStore needs.

blocked_by_product_defects.summary: Re-applying an identical write inserts a duplicate and trips a UNIQUE index, observed across atelier_command_corpus_entry, atelier_command_corpus_blocked, atelier_export_result and atelier_story_card. Check-then-act SurrealQL replaced atomic PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT. Mechanism undetermined. Any restored idempotency test will hit this until it is fixed in src/. Needs its own src/-owning microtask.

Loom edge creation and block updates are not ledger-backed. src/storage/surreal/loom_store.rs create_loom_edge (lines 1193-1388, 195 lines) contains no kernel_event_ledger / append_kernel_event / NewKernelEvent reference; update_loom_block (964-977) likewise. The event type KNOWLEDGE_LOOM_TAG_MUTATED exists only as a stringified variant (src/kernel/mod.rs:395) and is never emitted by any code path.
blocked_by_product_defects.manual_drift: src/user_manual/seed.rs:1117 documents KNOWLEDGE_LOOM_TAG_MUTATED as emitted with aggregate_type=loom_edge, aggregate_id=edge_id. The in-product manual promises an event the product does not produce (HBR-MAN currency defect in addition to the missing receipt).
blocked_by_product_defects.consequence: Five restoration items cannot be ported: there is no receipt to assert and nothing to roll back. mt023_tag_edge_create_appends_atomic_receipt_and_survives_restart, mt023_tag_edge_create_rolls_back_when_ledger_append_fails, mt024_favorite_mutation_appends_atomic_receipt_and_survives_restart, mt024_favorite_mutation_rolls_back_when_ledger_append_fails, mt024_mention_edge_backlink_is_atomic_and_survives_restart.
blocked_by_product_defects.verified_by: KERNEL_BUILDER-20260910-073935 (fn-body extraction at the implementation layer, not the database.rs trait wrappers)
blocked_by_product_defects.routing: src/ defect; needs its own microtask. The five tests should be restored by that microtask once the edge/favorite paths append their receipts atomically.

blocked_by_product_defects.summary: Submitting the identical memory-capsule record twice through SurrealKernelActionSubmitter is REJECTED by the EventLedger rather than collapsed: the recorder reuses the same idempotency key but produces a different payload hash on the second submission, so the ledger's fail-closed divergence guard fires. Identical input must yield an identical idempotent payload; something non-deterministic (timestamp, fresh id, or ordering) is being folded into the payload the recorder declares idempotent.
blocked_by_product_defects.ledger_error_verbatim: Rejected(KernelActionRejection { code: kernel_event_ledger_append_failed, reason: appending memory action to EventLedger failed: conflict: kernel event idempotency key was reused with different event content; idempotency_key=memory_capsule_record:<capsule_id>:<sha256>; existing_payload_hash=bb501fd6...; new_payload_hash=321b9571...; existing_aggregate_type=memory_capsule; new_aggregate_type=memory_capsule; same aggregate_id })
blocked_by_product_defects.distinct_from: DEF-SYSTEMIC-UPSERT-IDEMPOTENCY (check-then-act creates duplicates). Here the ledger correctly refuses; the defect is upstream in the recorder's payload construction.
blocked_by_product_defects.corroboration: src/storage/surreal/mt136_kernel_action_submitter_proof.rs, the in-source proof of this same submitter, is RED in suite-run-1 (MT-141 evidence).
blocked_by_product_defects.exact_field_not_traced: The non-deterministic field was not isolated in this session (action definition at src/kernel/action_catalog.rs:398; submitter path under src/storage/surreal/). Left for the owning src/ microtask.
blocked_by_product_defects.routing: src/ defect; needs its own microtask. The restored test stays in place and red as the acceptance proof for that fix.
